stories.headline: FED HOLDS AT 3.50%-3.75% BUT THREE HAWKISH DISSENTS RATTLE CHAIR WARSH'S SECOND MEETING
stories.body: The FOMC voted 9-3 Wednesday to hold rates, with Cleveland's Beth Hammack, Minneapolis's Neel Kashkari, and Dallas's Lorie Logan all dissenting in favor of a quarter-point hike - the most dissents of Kevin Warsh's young chairmanship - while the post-meeting statement, again shorter than the pre-Warsh norm, cited elevated uncertainty tied to the Middle East conflict.
stories.explain: Three simultaneous dissents on a hold decision is a rare, meaningful signal: it tells markets the committee itself is split on whether recent inflation and oil-driven price pressure justify tightening now rather than waiting, not just that one regional president disagrees. Warsh's terse statement style, paired with his public framing of inflation as 'a choice,' leaves markets short on forward guidance right as oil just spiked 6.6% on fresh Iran strikes - exactly the kind of shock that could firm up the hawks' case by September. Fed funds futures will do the real work of repricing over the next few sessions as traders decide whether today's 9-3 split is a one-off or the start of a more contentious back half of the year.

stories.headline: NASDAQ 100 EXTENDS CORRECTION, FALLS 2.06% AS FED DISSENTS AND OIL SPIKE COLLIDE HOURS BEFORE MEGA-CAP EARNINGS
stories.body: The NDX dropped 568 points to 27,192.31, now more than 11% below its June peak and deeper in correction territory, as three hawkish FOMC dissents and a 6.6% jump in WTI crude combined to pressure long-duration growth names just hours before Microsoft and Meta report earnings after the close.
stories.explain: Nasdaq 100 constituents are priced heavily on cash flows expected years out, which makes them unusually sensitive to the real discount rate used to value them; both a hawkish dissent shock and an oil-driven inflation shock push that discount rate up, which mechanically lowers the present value of distant AI-capex-funded earnings even before any single company reports. Today's move stacks two separate discount-rate shocks - policy-path uncertainty from Warsh's Fed and a war-risk premium in oil - onto an index already down 11% from its peak on capex-efficiency doubts. That combination raises the bar for tonight's Microsoft and Meta prints: strong headline numbers may not be enough to stop the slide if capex guidance doesn't also address the tighter-for-longer risk the bond market just repriced.

stories.headline: WTI CRUDE SURGES 6.6% TO $84.46 AS IRAN RESUMES STRIKES ON U.S. FORCES, SHATTERING A BRIEF CEASEFIRE
stories.body: WTI crude settled up 6.6% at $84.46 a barrel and Brent jumped 7.9% to $90.74 after Iran's Revolutionary Guard launched ballistic missiles at U.S. forces, ending a days-long pause in the conflict; President Trump told Fox News Iran 'is going to get a beating,' reviving the war-risk premium that had eased earlier in the week.
stories.explain: Oil's war-risk premium reflects the market pricing a probability-weighted chance of supply disruption - through direct damage to production, sanctions escalation, or a shipping chokepoint like the Strait of Hormuz - rather than any change in current physical supply or demand today. A single day's 6-8% swing of this size shows how quickly that probability can be repriced when a ceasefire breaks rather than holds, and it matters beyond energy trading floors because oil feeds directly into headline CPI within a month or two. That pass-through is exactly why this move lands on the same day as three FOMC dissents favoring a hike - a sustained oil shock is the kind of input that turns a split committee into a majority for tightening.

stories.headline: MICROSOFT, META REPORT AFTER THE BELL WITH FY27 CAPEX GUIDANCE THE REAL SWING FACTOR, NOT THE HEADLINE BEAT
stories.body: Microsoft is expected to post EPS of $4.24 (+16% YoY) on revenue of $87.62 billion (+15%) after guiding to roughly $190 billion in 2026 capex, while Meta is expected to post EPS of $7.18 on revenue of $60.22 billion (+27%) after raising its own capex outlook to $125-145 billion; with beat odds near 95% already priced in for both, investors are focused almost entirely on forward capex commentary.
stories.explain: When beat probability is already priced at 95%, a headline EPS or revenue beat carries almost no new information for the stock - the entire distribution of possible price reactions gets compressed into how management talks about next year's spending relative to this year's, since that's the one number the market hasn't already absorbed. Capex guidance functions like forward guidance does for a central bank: it's the market's best available read on whether depreciation from today's AI buildout will keep outrunning the revenue it's meant to generate. With the Nasdaq 100 already down 11% from its peak on exactly this capex-efficiency question, tonight's commentary carries more weight than it would in a calmer tape.

stories.headline: GOLD RISES TOWARD $4,066 AS IRAN ESCALATION AND A SPLIT FED LIFT HAVEN DEMAND DESPITE A SOFTER DOLLAR MOVE
stories.body: Gold gained about 0.9% to roughly $4,066 an ounce, extending its advance as renewed Iran strikes and Wednesday's divided 9-3 FOMC vote added to macro uncertainty even though the dollar index fell only modestly to 101.30.
stories.explain: Gold's move today reflects two haven-demand triggers stacking rather than reinforcing through the usual dollar channel: a weaker dollar normally makes gold cheaper for foreign buyers and explains part of a rally, but the modest 0.25% DXY decline here is too small to account for a 0.9% gold gain on its own. The gap is filled by direct safe-haven positioning - renewed war risk in the Middle East and a Fed that just showed real internal disagreement both raise the odds investors assign to a disorderly outcome, and gold carries no yield, so it becomes relatively more attractive whenever that tail risk grows regardless of what real rates are doing. Watch whether gold keeps climbing if oil holds its gains overnight; a Fed forced toward the hawks' view by sustained oil-driven inflation would be a genuine headwind for bullion even amid rising geopolitical risk.

stories.headline: OHIO STATE SIGNS RECORD $17 MILLION-A-YEAR JERSEY PATCH DEAL WITH JPMORGANCHASE AS SPONSORSHIP ARMS RACE ESCALATES
stories.body: Ohio State announced a jersey patch sponsorship with JPMorganChase reportedly worth around $17 million per year, one of two record-setting patch deals unveiled this week alongside Illinois's five-year, $30 million pact with Busey Bank, underscoring how quickly athlete-facing revenue deals are scaling across college basketball programs; separately, Purdue opened preseason play with a 79-48 win over Calgary behind 14 points from Antoine West Jr.

stories.headline: WARRIORS RE-SIGN DRAYMOND GREEN TO A ONE-YEAR, $27.7 MILLION DEAL AS BUCKS EMERGE AS FAVORITES FOR PEYTON WATSON
stories.body: Golden State re-signed Draymond Green to a one-year, $27.7 million contract to keep its core intact, while Milwaukee is viewed as the favorite to retain restricted free agent Peyton Watson using a $25.5 million trade exception after Denver's five-year, $70 million offer sheet; the Lakers and Cavaliers are separately pursuing free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga.

stories.headline: FALCONS' BIJAN ROBINSON AND LIONS' JAHMYR GIBBS HOLD OUT OF CAMP SEEKING NEW DEALS AS MARKET-SETTING CONTRACTS PILE UP
stories.body: Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson and Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs are both sitting out training camp practices in pursuit of contract extensions, a standoff playing out against a week that has already produced Jalen Carter's four-year, $152 million deal with Philadelphia and Denzel Ward's two-year, $62.2 million extension with Cleveland; all 32 teams have now opened camp for the 2026 season.

stories.headline: BIG TEN MEDIA DAYS DAY TWO: OHIO STATE AND OREGON HEADLINE AS THREE STRAIGHT DIFFERENT CHAMPIONS RESHAPE THE CONFERENCE
stories.body: Ohio State, Oregon, Michigan State, Minnesota, Purdue, and UCLA took the stage Wednesday for day two of Big Ten Media Days in Chicago, with Oregon entering as a popular pick to finally break through after four strong seasons under Dan Lanning and defending national champion Indiana's stunning 2025 turnaround still looming over the conversation after three consecutive titles went to three different Big Ten programs.

sports.detail: Recruiting remains the offseason focus with recent commitments from a 4-star cornerback and a 4-star safety highlighted in this week's roundups; Jedd Fisch continues calling plays himself heading into year three. The Huskies open the season Sunday, Sept. 6, at home against Washington State.

The full roster has now arrived on Montlake, with commit Wini Braga working out alongside center Lathan Sommerville after questions earlier this summer about his commitment. Danny Sprinkle is rebuilding after Hannes Steinbach was taken 14th overall by the Charlotte Hornets in the NBA Draft.

The defending Super Bowl champions held a public Day 4 practice Tuesday at Virginia Mason Athletic Center, with Jalen Milroe turning in his best day of camp and Cooper Kupp making a highlight-reel catch; the team is still without pads, which arrive Thursday, and has no new injury news to report. Seattle opens the season Sept. 9 at home against New England in a Super Bowl LX rematch.

The restricted free agency stalemate with center Jalen Duren continues, though league sources now believe momentum favors Duren staying in Detroit after 'modest' progress in talks; the Pistons continue to reject sign-and-trade scenarios. Duren is coming off a career year - 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds a game - that helped power Detroit to 60 wins.

Dominic Canzone's tiebreaking two-run homer in the eighth inning - his second of the game and fifth of the series - rallied Seattle past the Dodgers 7-6 on Tuesday. The two teams play game two of the series Wednesday night at Dodger Stadium, first pitch 10:10 PM ET / 7:10 PM PT.

watchlist: Microsoft and Meta report earnings after the bell Wednesday, Apple and Amazon Thursday — FY27 capex guidance is the real swing factor with ~95% beat odds already priced in
Iran-U.S. conflict escalation — watch for further strikes or Strait of Hormuz risk after Wednesday's missile attack reignited the oil war-risk premium
Three FOMC dissents (Hammack, Kashkari, Logan) favoring a hike — watch positioning shift into the September meeting
Mariners at Dodgers, game two of the series — Wednesday 7:10 PM PT, Dodger Stadium
Jalen Duren restricted free agency stalemate with the Pistons remains unresolved

deepDive.title: Why Three Fed Dissents and a 6.6% Oil Spike Are the Same Story: Pass-Through and the Fed's Core-vs-Headline Problem
content: Today packed two shocks that look separate but are mechanically linked: WTI crude jumped 6.6% to $84.46 on renewed Iran strikes, and the same afternoon the FOMC held rates 9-3 with three officials - Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan - dissenting in favor of a hike. Those events are not coincidental neighbors on the calendar; they are the same underlying tension expressing itself in two markets at once. Oil shocks are the fastest-moving input into U.S. inflation data of almost any single commodity, and a Fed that is already internally split over whether current price pressure justifies tightening now has just been handed a fresh, sizable reason for the hawks on the committee to push harder.

The mechanism runs through what economists call pass-through: a sustained rise in crude flows into gasoline and diesel prices within days, into airfares and shipping costs within weeks, and eventually into a wide range of goods prices that depend on transportation costs, typically showing up in headline CPI within one to two reporting cycles. The Fed's preferred gauge, core PCE, strips out food and energy specifically because oil shocks are often temporary and reverse - but 'often' is not 'always,' and a committee deciding how much weight to put on a supply-side shock versus underlying demand is exactly the debate that produces three simultaneous dissents rather than the usual none or one.

The clearest historical parallel is the 1970s oil shocks, when the Fed under Arthur Burns treated OPEC-driven price spikes as transitory and kept policy loose, only to watch energy costs embed into wage- and price-setting behavior broadly enough that inflation became self-sustaining rather than temporary - a mistake later chairs spent a decade unwinding. Today's dissent count doesn't mean Warsh's Fed is repeating that error, but it does mean at least three sitting officials are unwilling to bet on this oil shock being purely transitory, especially layered on top of a Middle East conflict that had already been elevating energy prices intermittently for weeks before today's escalation.

For a portfolio watching this week's calendar, the read-through is that Wednesday's oil spike raises the bar for what would need to happen at the September meeting to keep the committee at 9-3 rather than tipping toward a majority for a hike - a sustained Brent price above $90 into the next CPI print would hand the hawks exactly the data they'd need. That same dynamic is what's compressing Nasdaq 100 valuations today, since a Fed forced toward tightening by oil-driven inflation raises the discount rate applied to Microsoft's and Meta's long-dated AI capex bets before either company even reports tonight's numbers.
